claim: The EPP architecture proposal explicitly designates the Data Layer as the layer accessed by all others and as an extensible layer intended for customization, while the Ext-Proc Server is deliberately non-extensible.
stance_target: the data layer is the correct architectural seam for adding non-k8s-pod backends
scope_conditions: GIE proposal 0683, status Implemented, authored by @kfswain
quoted_support: The Data Layer is of note, as it is a vertical that will be accessed by all the others.

claim: Extending the Data Layer's Model Server Protocol comes with an explicit portability trade-off acknowledged by the project itself.
stance_target: cost of customizing the data layer
quoted_support: Many extensions to scheduling will require changes to ingested metrics, as such, the data layer will be built to be extended, but extenders accept that the Model Server Protocol will no longer provide guarantees on portability of a model server out of the box.

claim: The proposal explicitly advises against modifying the Ext-Proc Server layer because deviation from the well-defined ext_proc protocol could make the EPP unusable or unstable.
stance_target: customization should target the Data/Routing/Scheduling layers, not the ext-proc transport itself
quoted_support: The Ext-Proc Server protocol is very well defined & specific, deviation could cause the EPP to become unusable or unstable. Extension is ill-advised.
